To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

planet-hosts stars have a systematically higher metal content than non planet-host stars, that there is a statistically significative abundance separation between the thick and thin disc stars, and that the chemical composition of the thin and thick disc populations is not clearly separated.

planet-bearing stars are more metal-rich than stars without planets, that the chemical evolution of planet-bearing stars is similar to stars without planets, and that the chemical evolution trends of stars in the thick disc are different from those in the thin disc.
planet host stars show a higher metallicity compared to non-host stars, and that the galactic chemical enrichment trends for stars with and without planetary companions are similar.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed study of the chemical properties of the stars with planets.
the study of the chemical properties of the stars that are most similar to the Sun and the study of the differences between the abundancies of stars with and stars without planets.
the study of the galactic chemical history of stars with planetary companions, as well as with stars in the thin disc and the thick disc.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence of a chemical separation between planet host and non planet host stars.
the planet formation process does not appear to depend strongly on the chemical composition of the star.
there is no significant chemical difference between stars with and without detected planets, and also no significant difference between the thick and thin disc stars.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
planet-host stars are not chemically different to non-planet-hosts.
the planet-hosting stars are not different from the stars without planets, except for the higher average metallicity.
the stars that harbour planetary companions are simply the stars with the highest metallicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
planet-hosting stars are not a chemically distinct sample of the galactic disc, but they are simply the high metallicity stars of the galactic thin disc.
there are no differences between the chemical abundances and the galactic chemical trends of planet hosts and stars without planets.
the planet-hosts are a subset of stars from a given metallicity distribution.
